task_suitability.task: change-slot: move Saturday 17 October 09:20 to 14:20 and return to the confirm step
task_suitability.evidence: probes/14/probe.json: final url /confirm.html, slot '14:20 to 14:40', vehicle and waste kept

strengths.title: After a slot change, 'Next' returns straight to 'Check and book' with the day, the new slot, the vehicle and the waste all kept, so a resident moving a slot does not re-enter the car or the waste

candidates.title: 'Change slot' opens a blank 'Book a slot' page with no trace of the booking being changed
candidates.description: A change action should open the chooser on the current choice and say what is kept. Here, on the confirm page, 'Change slot' links to a bare index.html. The page that opens is the generic first step, 'Book a slot', with 'Today' pressed and an empty Slots area. Saturday 17 and 09:20 are not shown as the current choice. Nothing says this is a change to an existing booking, or that the vehicle (Car) and waste (Garden waste, Wood) will be kept.
candidates.impact: A resident moving a slot may believe their booking has been discarded and that they must start again. They may re-enter vehicle and waste details or abandon the change. They also have to re-pick a day they wanted to keep.

scope.persona: resident changing the slot mid-booking, on a phone

evidence.detail: click 'Change slot' -> url http://127.0.0.1:4701/index.html (no query); heading 'Book a slot'; 'Today' [pressed]; Slots group empty; no text about an existing booking

factor_notes.frequency: Every slot change from the confirm step goes through this link; 'Residents changing a booking' are a declared user group, and the change-slot journey is core.
factor_notes.impact: Context loss at the first step of the change; the persona's stated unknown (are the other details kept?) is left unanswered and the screen suggests a restart.
factor_notes.persistence: Occurs on every change; experience may teach a repeat user that the rest is kept, but residents book only a few times a year.

candidates.recommendation: Open the chooser with the current day and slot selected. Show a line such as 'Changing your Saturday 17 October booking; your vehicle and waste are kept'.

candidates.title: 'Few left' slots are shown first, out of time order and without a heading, splitting 14:00 from 14:20
candidates.description: A list of times people look up by clock time should read in time order, with any grouping labelled. With Saturday 17 chosen at 375 px, the first grid under 'Slots' is an unlabelled block of the 'Few left' times: 08:20, 08:40, 09:00, 09:40, 10:20, 10:40, 13:40, 14:00, 15:00 and 16:40. Only after it come the 'Morning' and 'Afternoon' headings with the remaining times. Someone reading the first grid sees 14:00 followed by 15:00, with no 14:20. 14:20 appears further down, under 'Afternoon', below the fold. The ARIA snapshot lists the slots in time order under 'Morning' and 'Afternoon', so the visual order differs from the reading and focus order.
candidates.impact: A resident looking for a particular time may conclude it is taken and settle for the wrong slot or give up. A keyboard user's focus order may also jump around the visual layout.

scope.persona: resident changing the slot mid-booking, on a phone

evidence.detail: full-page capture: unlabelled 'Few left' block above 'Morning'; Afternoon grid lacks 13:40, 14:00, 15:00, 16:40
group 'Slots' lists heading Morning, 08:00 ... 11:40, heading Afternoon, 12:00 ... 17:20 in time order
14:20 reached only after scrolling past the Few-left block and the Morning block (step-04.png)

factor_notes.frequency: Every day with 'Few left' slots; on Saturday 17, 10 of the 22 free slots are pulled out of order.
factor_notes.impact: Affects anyone looking for a specific time; the persona may pick a wrong slot, with no loss of data.
factor_notes.persistence: Recurs on every visit; a repeat user may learn to scroll on.

candidates.recommendation: Keep every slot in time order under Morning and Afternoon, and mark scarcity on each slot in place.
